idiom_name: typed EventEmitter listener + KafkaJS consumer.run({ eachMessage }) handler
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits Node's event loop, so the consumer is a typed listener function: emitter.on('order', (o: Order) => ...) - declaration merging or a generic EventEmitter<T> types the event/payload pairs - and broker clients are typed at the handler boundary, with KafkaJS's consumer.run({ eachMessage: async ({ topic, partition, message }) => ... }) handing one message to the function while owning fetch, offsets and heartbeats. Types add the contract the classic listener interface used to carry but do not change the delivery model; keep an explicit listener interface when the callback must expose more than one method (ack/nack/close) or when adapting an untyped client.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: message.value is untrusted bytes - parse and validate before treating it as the declared payload type.
KafkaJS eachMessage blocks the partition; exceeding sessionTimeout without heartbeat/pause drops the consumer from the group.
A typed EventEmitter only checks call sites against the event map - a wrong name or a missing listener still compiles, so keep the map in one module.
An unhandled 'error' event on the client emitter crashes the process.
